question: Which cup has a higher concentration of sugar?
background: Passive transport occurs when a substance passes through the cell membrane without needing any energy to pass through. This happens when a substance moves from an area where it is more concentrated to an area where it is less concentrated. Concentration is the number of particles of a substance in a given volume. Let's say you dissolve a teaspoon of salt in a cup of water. Then you dissolve two teaspoons of salt in another cup of water. The second solution will have a higher concentration of salt.
situation: A man put two cups, cup A and cup B, filled with equal amounts of water on to a table and walked away to go check his mail. His son came along and saw the two cups and decided to put some sugar in them to make a tasty drink. The child poured two spoonfuls of sugar into cup A and three spoonfuls of sugar into cup B.
Mis_reasoning: Step 1: Both cups started with equal amounts of water, so the comparison depends on how the sugar affects the concentration in each cup. Step 2: The background explains that concentration is about how particles spread in a given volume, and passive transport tends to move substances from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated. Step 3: Since cup B has three spoonfuls of sugar, the sugar particles are more crowded and will spread out more through the water than in cup A. Step 4: When the particles spread out more, they become less concentrated in any one part of the cup, while cup A with only two spoonfuls stays more compact. Step 5: Therefore, even though cup B has more total sugar, cup A ends up with the higher concentration of sugar.
